_comment: Bifrost config skeleton for Heimdall. Placeholders only, no real keys. During the live run the actual method used (this file OR the web UI) is recorded in RUN_REPORT.md at Checkpoint 3. Model names here mirror .env; they are the only place outside .env that names a model because this is Bifrost's allowlist config, not a harness script. Roles run narrowest to widest by FUNCTION, not seniority: interpreter, reporter, clerk. Model tiers are routine/standard/restricted, named for ACCESS LEVEL, not cost.

keys._comment: One throwaway provider key with a provider-side spend cap. Injected from OPENAI_API_KEY at load time. Never commit the real value.

virtual_keys.name: interpreter
virtual_keys._comment: NARROWEST role. Routine tier only. Budget deliberately tiny so Block 5 can exhaust it in a few calls.

virtual_keys.name: clerk
virtual_keys._comment: WIDEST role. All three models. Clerk audits the case live; if the clerk cannot see something, court stops.

_stubs._comment: STUB list from the PRD. Named here so the article can say plainly what was NOT built. None of these are implemented this pass.
_stubs.key_revocation_mid_run: STUB: would revoke a virtual key mid-run and confirm calls stop. Only if Block 5 finishes early.
_stubs.teams_and_customers: STUB: would add a department-level budget layer above the individual badges.
_stubs.sso_oidc: STUB: would wire an OIDC identity provider so badges map to real identities.
_stubs.rate_limits: STUB: would set token_max_limit and request_max_limit per virtual key and test throttling.
_stubs.multi_provider_failover: STUB: would add a second provider and test failover when the first is unavailable.
_stubs.second_provider: STUB: no second provider is configured. OpenAI only this pass.
